about.title: Lincoln Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a fatal collision happens on a Lincoln road, the days after are overwhelming — funeral arrangements, insurance calls, and unanswered questions about what happened. Placer County's public crash data shows dozens of injury collisions each year on corridors like Twelve Bridges Drive and Joiner Parkway, with reported crashes clustering on Friday afternoons as commuters and school traffic overlap. When a collision proves fatal, California law gives certain family members a limited window and a defined path to pursue accountability through a civil claim, separate from any police investigation or criminal matter. We handle wrongful death claims directly. Our team can review what happened, explain who may have standing to file, and walk your family through next steps — all on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Families in Lincoln Should Know

items.title: Standing Is Limited by Law
items.desc: California restricts who may bring a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, then extending to certain dependents or heirs if none exist. We can help sort out who qualifies before time runs short.

items.title: The Clock Starts Right Away
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity (such as a public road authority) carry a much shorter deadline. Acting early preserves evidence and options.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Immediate Costs
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the family has lost, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance — losses that are real even though they're hard to put a number on.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those relatives exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be able to bring the claim. Because this can get complicated, especially in blended families, it's worth having us review your specific situation.

items.question: Is there something different about pursuing a claim if the crash happened on a Lincoln city street?
items.answer: If a public road or intersection in Lincoln — such as one along Lincoln Boulevard or Ferrari Ranch Road — is found to have contributed to the crash, a claim against the city or county may involve a much shorter filing deadline than the standard two years. That's one reason it helps to speak with us soon after a fatal collision rather than waiting.

items.question: Is there a charge to review my case?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews — there's no charge to you upfront. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your family recovers compensation.
